- Model consistently underestimates prices in early-to-mid forecast horizon (especially 1–7 days ahead), especially when prices are trending down.
- Overestimates prices after sharp upward spikes (e.g., 90+ → 95+), often overshooting by 2–5% and failing to correct.
- Underestimates prices during mean-reversion phases, particularly when recent history shows downward momentum.
- Shows persistent lag in responding to recent price drops — forecasts remain too high for 3–5 days after a sharp decline.
- Tends to overfit recent high volatility periods, leading to erratic forecasts when prices stabilize.
- When history includes a strong upward trend, model often fails to capture the full magnitude of the trend, underestimating peak values.
- Forecasts are more accurate when the 30-day history is stable or trending upward — less accurate during volatile or downward transitions.
- Model exhibits bias toward lower values when the true outcome is above 85, especially in the first 10 days of forecast horizon.
